newsitem.title: POLAND: BOXING-GOLOTA GETS SUSPENDED JAIL TERM FOR 1990 BRAWL.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-GOLOTA GETS SUSPENDED JAIL TERM FOR 1990 BRAWL.

text.p: A Polish court handed down a suspended two year jail term and a $7,000 fine to heavyweight boxer Andrzej Golota on Thursday after he returned to his homeland to face the music over a restaurant brawl seven years ago.
Golota, 28, is looking forward to a bright career in the United States, although he last year twice squandered likely victories against U.S. rival Riddick Bowe by landing low blows.

Golota had not dared return to Poland because he was wanted by police over the May 1990 events in a Wloclawek restaurant, but finally decided to face a Polish court after getting official guarantees he would not face instant arrest.

His wife Mariola Golota said the couple wanted to get back to the United States as fast as possible and Andrzej was planning new fights although he was still recovering from jaw injuries, from his last clash with Bowe..
Golota was accused of beating a stranger, Pawel Bialostocki, and robbing him of his shirt, trousers and a shoe in a restaurant in Wloclawek, central Poland.
Golota expressed regret and apologised to Bialostocki in court.
